Audio Priority Bar 2.12.0 adds profiles, keyboard control of the whole panel, a microphone order of its own for headphones, and controls for a Jabra headset's noise mode, sidetone and busylight. Picking a device now keeps automatic switching on. Coming from 2.11.0, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Picking a device

- Picking a device in the panel, from Shortcuts, or with **Output only**, **Mic only** and **Use both** now keeps automatic switching on, as a pick in Control Center already did. Before, a pick turned automatic switching off until you turned it back on ([#66](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/66), [#68](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/68)).
- Your pick stays until it disconnects or a device your list would pick connects, so a headset you plug in during a call still takes over. A USB microphone or a virtual device appearing no longer ends it ([#69](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/69)).
- The panel says when your pick is holding. To keep a pick for good, turn automatic switching off.

## Profiles

- Profiles keep their own Speakers, Headphones and Microphones orders and whether automatic switching is on. Add them in **Settings › Profiles**, then switch from the menu in the panel heading, from Settings, from the **Apply Profile** shortcut, or with a Focus filter, which goes back to the previous profile when the Focus ends ([#63](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/63)).

## Microphones

- **Microphones follow the output**, in **Settings › Devices** and off by default, gives headphones their own microphone order, so moving from headphones to speakers can also move to your desk microphone ([#62](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/62)).

## Jabra headsets

- A Jabra headset behind a Link dongle gets its noise control (Off, Noise Cancellation or HearThrough), sidetone and busylight right on its row. A call keeps the busylight on until it ends, and a call started with the headset's call button ends from the row ([#70](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/70)).
- **Light a Jabra headset's busylight while an app uses its microphone**, in Settings and off by default, covers calls in apps that don't signal one, such as Meet or Teams in a browser.
- Tested on an Evolve2 85 behind a Link 380. Other Jabra headsets behind a Link dongle should work from Jabra's own setting definitions, and an issue naming the model you tried helps confirm it.

## Menu bar

- **Red while automatic switching is off**, in **Settings › Icon** and off by default, turns the icon red as a reminder to turn it back on. Thanks to Dave Smith for this one ([#65](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/65)).

## Keyboard

- The whole panel now works from the keyboard: Up and Down move through every item, Return or Space acts on it, and Left and Right change levels and step through profiles ([#64](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/64)).
- **Forget Device** asks for confirmation again, and text fields have Copy, Paste and Undo.

## Updates

- Updating from 2.9.0 or later downloads only what changed. Older versions download the full archive.

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Connecting a Bluetooth device from the panel asks for Bluetooth permission, and Accessibility is optional, for the hover preview. Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
